direction: Make coherent cluster moves that preserve intra-cluster contacts exactly. Build the contact graph from pairs within 1e-6 of the maximum, partition it into 6-10 communities by spectral clustering on the graph Laplacian (or by greedy modularity on the Gram matrix), and repeatedly pick one community and rotate all its points rigidly by an angle drawn from 0.03-0.25 radians in a random coordinate 2-plane, optionally counter-rotating a neighbouring community; a rigid rotation preserves every intra-cluster cosine while changing only inter-cluster pairs, so the move rewires the contact topology without the internal damage caused by independent Gaussian point noise. idea: Delete the most overloaded or rattler points to create under-constrained N-1/N-2 intermediates, LP-polish the hole open, reinsert via largest-void search, and alternate with N+2 grow-then-prune cycles.
direction: Change topology through an N-1 intermediate rather than kicking the 180-point jam. Delete the single most overloaded point (largest contact count, tie-broken by largest sum of near-max cosines), LP-polish the resulting 179-point code until its maximum drops clearly below 0.4623, then find its largest spherical void by dense random sampling plus refinement and insert the 180th point there before a full LP polish; in alternating cycles instead delete a rattler and a high-contact point, or build a 182-point code and delete its two worst points. Removing a point creates a genuinely different, under-constrained contact graph whose reinsertion point need not recreate the deleted point's contacts, unlike small shakes of the intact configuration. Reserve at most 100 seconds for all deletion cycles and 40 seconds for final polishing.

direction: Search a symmetry-constrained basin from scratch, then break the symmetry. Optimise only 90 unit representatives a_i in R^9 for the antipodal code {a_i, -a_i}, whose maximum cosine is max over i<j of |<a_i, a_j>|, using batched annealed LogSumExp Adam (several random and D9-root-seeded starts run simultaneously as a (B,90,9) tensor, exponent annealed from about 30 to 500 over roughly 2000 steps), then expand to 180 points, release the antipodal constraint with a small tangential perturbation of one member of each pair, and LP-polish the full code; if the record is already near-antipodal this still explores a different constrained optimum, and if the symmetric optimum approaches 0.462 the symmetry-breaking step can push below it. Keep this self-contained search under 120 seconds, compare against a loaded copy of best.npy, and always return the better of the two after the final polish.

idea: Target-feasibility trust-region LP that minimizes total slack violation of <xi,xj><=t for infeasible targets below the record with rotating excluded stressed contacts to force topology changes, followed by ordinary minimax LP polish.
direction: Use target-feasibility search rather than repeatedly minimising $t$ from the incumbent: set targets such as $t=0.4620$, $0.4615$, and $0.4610$, linearise only pairs with cosine above $t-0.01$ (capped at the 800 tightest), and solve trust-region LPs that minimise total violation of $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\le t$ subject to tangent constraints and radius $0.01$–$0.03$; after each solve, renormalise, drop satisfied pairs, add newly violated pairs, and use LP dual values to identify and deliberately break the most stressed contacts by excluding a rotating subset of them for several iterations. Cycle through targets and random excluded-contact subsets under a hard internal deadline of about 150 seconds, keeping the best fully evaluated configuration and reserving the final time for one ordinary LP polish, so that the method searches directly for a different feasible topology instead of sliding back to the record's vertex.

direction: Exploit the rattlers with frozen-core, subset-only surgery. Identify the 2 zero-contact points plus points with at most 3 contacts at threshold 1e-7, freeze the other approximately 175 points, and relocate the free points one at a time by maximising their minimum angle to the frozen set using 200,000 random sphere samples followed by local tangential hill-climbing; then unfreeze only each relocated point and its 30-40 nearest neighbours (cosine above about 0.30) and run the trust-region LP on that subset of roughly 350 variables while the core stays fixed. Cycle the free points a few times, accept only true full-score improvements, then run one full LP polish, with all loops checking a hard internal deadline of 160 seconds and the incumbent returned immediately thereafter. This uses the genuine free degrees of freedom without perturbing the 1000+ contact core that all previous kicks destroyed.

idea: Cyclic orbit symmetry search with 20 seeds expanded by 9 rolls then symmetry breaking and free polish
direction: Search first in a symmetry-reduced space, then break the symmetry: parameterise 20 seed vectors in $\mathbb{R}^9$ and generate all 180 points by applying the nine cyclic coordinate permutations to each seed, giving exactly $20\times9$ points; optimise only the 180 seed parameters with annealed LogSumExp Adam, evaluating the full $180\times9$ Gram matrix at each step, and optionally add small sign-flip variants if they preserve the count exactly. Once this highly structured code is locally optimal, release all 180 points independently, add a tiny deterministic symmetry-breaking perturbation of size $10^{-3}$–$10^{-2}$, optimise freely, and finish with LP polish; include an immediate shape/count assertion and fallback to `best.npy` if construction fails, addressing the earlier antipodal implementation crash while testing whether the record lacks a hidden group-orbit organisation.

Run several short random restarts rather than one long run, rank local optima not only by maximum cosine but also by contact-degree variance, number of rattlers, and isotropy error $\|\sum_i x_ix_i^\top-20I\|_F$, and subject only the most balanced few candidates to short LP polishes; reserve the last 20–25 seconds for polishing the overall best candidate and return the incumbent if any stage approaches the deadline.

direction: Perform properly localised delete-and-rebuild surgery: remove the two rattlers plus 8–15 highest-degree or randomly chosen hub points, LP-polish the remaining 165–170 points until their internal maximum drops materially, then reinsert the removed points one at a time at the best of at least 20,000 random candidate voids followed by local random refinement; after each insertion, optimise only the inserted point and neighbours with cosine above $0.25$ using a few hundred fixed steps of tangential Adam, and run a full LP polish only after all points have been restored. Repeat with different deleted sets chosen from high-degree points, rattlers, and random points, but enforce strict clocks—for example, stop surgery by 110 seconds, perform the final polish by 165 seconds, and always retain the loaded best configuration as a fallback—because this topology-changing idea is promising only if its previously observed timeout failure is eliminated.

idea: Enforce exact antipodal symmetry on 90 free vectors with LogSumExp Adam annealing then release symmetry with multi-scale tangent shakes plus annealed relaxation and LP polish.
direction: Test the missing-symmetry hypothesis with an exactly antipodal ansatz: parameterize only $Y\in\mathbb R^{90\times9}$, form $X=[Y;-Y]$, and optimize the LogSumExp of all distinct pair dots—including $y_i\cdot y_j$, $-y_i\cdot y_j$, and the fixed antipodal $-1$ pairs excluded—with projected Adam at inverse temperatures 30, 100, 300, and 800, learning rates $0.005,0.003,0.0015,0.0007$, and time-checked stages totaling at most 60 seconds. Then break the symmetry deliberately with Gaussian tangent noise of sizes $0,10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3}$ in separate branches, run 15 seconds of annealed softmax relaxation on the full 180 points, LP-polish each branch for at most 10 seconds, and keep the best; this determines whether enforcing 90 antipodal pairs finds a more regular basin before release, with `best.npy` as the timed fallback.

idea: LP-dual stress guided hub+rattler excision with frozen-core void resampling, annealed-softmax refinement and capped trust-region LP re-snapping.
direction: Use LP-dual stress to perform targeted graph surgery rather than random kicking: polish `best.npy` once with constraints capped at the 3000 tightest pairs, extract HiGHS inequality duals from `res.ineqlin.marginals` for slack $<10^{-7}$ pairs, aggregate dual weight per point, and remove the 4 highest-stress hub points plus both rattlers. Reinsert these 6 points one at a time against the frozen remaining points by scoring 60000 random unit vectors vectorially, locally refining the best 32 candidates with 300 projected-gradient steps on a temperature-annealed softmax of their dot products, and inserting the candidate with smallest true maximum dot; after each complete surgery run at most 8 seconds of capped LP polish and accept only a true improvement. Repeat with hub counts 3, 5, and 7 and dual-quantile choices under a hard 140-second exploration deadline, always retaining and returning the loaded best if no surgery improves it.

idea: Batched independent multi-start with annealed LogSumExp Adam plus diversity triage and capped trust-region LP finish.
direction: Run a genuinely record-independent, batched multi-start search to discover alternative contact graphs: create a $(24,180,9)$ NumPy tensor from 20 random Gaussian codes, 2 coordinate-permutation/sign variants of simple 9D constructions, and only 2 noisy record copies, then optimize all codes simultaneously with batched Gram matrices and annealed LogSumExp Adam, escalating inverse temperature from 20 to 500 over roughly 2500 steps while checking time every 25 steps. Rank finished codes by true maximum cosine and by a diversity signature consisting of sorted per-point contact counts at slack $10^{-4}$, select the best 3 mutually dissimilar codes, give each at most 15 seconds of constraint-capped LP polish, and reserve the final 25 seconds for polishing the overall winner; stop all exploration by 150 seconds and return the incumbent best if none wins.

idea: Rigid cluster rotations preserving intra-cluster Gram to change inter-cluster contact topology, plus rattler void relocation, masked softmax Adam, and short LP polish.
direction: Exploit the visible clustering through rigid cluster rotations that change inter-cluster contacts without disturbing intra-cluster geometry: build a graph using pair dots above 0.35, extract connected or greedily grown clusters of 4–18 points, choose a cluster with many contacts to outside points, and rotate only that cluster by $\exp(\theta(ab^\top-ba^\top))$ for orthonormal random $a,b$ and $\theta\in\{0.01,0.025,0.05,0.09\}$, which preserves every intra-cluster Gram entry exactly. Relocate the 2 rattlers afterward into the largest sampled voids, apply 400 steps of tangential softmax Adam to the moved cluster, rattlers, and their external contact neighbours while freezing the rest, then run at most 6 seconds of full LP polish and accept only an improvement; cycle through different clusters and rotation planes until 145 seconds, with strict per-attempt aborts and the original best returned if no rotation succeeds.

idea: Escape the jammed basin by repeatedly relocating overloaded hubs and cold rattlers into sampled large voids followed by fast annealed soft-max tangential repulsion, with annealing acceptance, then final trust-region LP polish.
LP-dual stress guided hub+rattler deletion with frozen-core greedy void reinsertion and capped trust-region LP acceptance.
direction: Use LP-dual stress to perform targeted graph surgery rather than random kicking: polish `best.npy` once with constraints capped at the 3000 tightest pairs, extract HiGHS inequality duals from `res.ineqlin.marginals` for slack $<10^{-7}$ pairs, aggregate dual weight per point, and remove the 4 highest-stress hub points plus both rattlers. Reinsert these 6 points one at a time against the frozen remaining points by scoring 60000 random unit vectors vectorially, locally refining the best 32 candidates with 300 projected-gradient steps on a temperature-annealed softmax of their dot products, and inserting the candidate with smallest true maximum dot; after each complete surgery run at most 8 seconds of capped LP polish and accept only a true improvement. Repeat with hub counts 3, 5, and 7 and dual-quantile choices under a hard 140-second exploration deadline, always retaining and returning the loaded best if no surgery improves it.
